text:
maya: heads-up — we need a quick decision on OTLP exporter behavior for inference services. Production incident this morning showed spans getting dropped on shutdown when requests were streaming.
chris: ugh. is this the async flush race again? which SDKs affected?
maya: python + rust + go. python service uses asyncio + batcher, rust service uses tokio + our otel-rs wrapper, go service uses the otel-go batcher. all three had partial traces for long streaming requests.
nana: (thanks for the ping) do we have an example span shape that was cut?
maya: yes — root span: `request.inference` -> child: `generate.tokens` for the streaming loop. on shutdown we got root closed before `generate.tokens` finished, exporter dropped child spans.
chris: so two problems: exporter flush on shutdown and parent end ordering. we should define a contract: exporters must be flushed before process exit, and SDK wrapper should await outstanding child spans.
nana: agreed. proposal: 1) add a language-agnostic "graceful_shutdown(timeout_ms)" API in our internal SDK shim that ensures batching exporter flush and waits for in-flight spans; 2) require instrumentation to end child spans before root end when streaming.
devon: +1 but need to be realistic about lang differences. in python we can `await tracer.force_flush()` on loop end. go has `Shutdown(ctx)` on the SDK. rust has `trace_provider.shutdown()` but async wait is tricky depending on runtime. we should ship small helper utilities per language.
chris: also need to adjust batching config — the batcher was configured aggressively for latency (batch size 1, delay 5ms). that meant more frequent exports and higher chance of in-flight export when process stops. can we increase `max_export_batch_size` and `schedule_delay_millis` for inference services? maybe env override: `REDWOOD_OTEL_BATCH_SIZE` and `REDWOOD_OTEL_SCHEDULE_MS`.
maya: yes add env overrides. but cost and retention constraints matter — larger batches reduce throughput spikes but increase memory. ops would want lower delay to see spans quickly for debug. maybe default medium (batch_size=256, schedule_ms=50) for inference tier, with per-service override.
nana: regardless, we need a unified span attribute contract so dashboards and retention policies can rely on consistent keys. propose standard attributes: `model.name`, `model.version`, `request.mode` (sync|stream), `tokens.generated`, `kv_cache.hit` (bool), `customer.id`, `route.id`.
chris: add `response.size_bytes` and `billing.unit_token_estimate` (string) so billing pipelines can sample-pull cost estimates from traces.
devon: note about attribute limits — otel servers drop >128 attributes. we must cap attribute cardinality: don't attach raw prompt text, only prompt_hash. also restrict `customer.id` to hashed id for PII.
maya: good call. also retention: we need to keep full traces for 7 days for debugging, aggregated metrics and span samples for 90 days. ingestion cost is a concern — maybe sample at 10% for standard customers, 100% for enterprise with SLA. sampling should be adaptive: do full sample on errors >5% or when rollback flags set.
chris: sampling needs to be implemented in SDK wrapper so it's consistent across languages. recommend probabilistic sampler at start of trace plus a deterministic override header (X-Redwood-Trace-Force) to force-sample for canaries.
nana: any blocking API changes? we need an init pattern to ensure the SDK wrapper is idempotent across language clients and doesn't re-register exporters. current bug: double-init in a few services causes duplicate spans.
devon: make init a no-op if already called and return a handle with `shutdown()` and `force_flush(timeout_ms)`. pseudo-python:

```
from redwood_otel import init, shutdown
handle = init(service_name="inference-embedder", batch_size=256)
# run server
await handle.force_flush(2000)  # ms
await handle.shutdown(5000)
```

for go/rust provide similar ergonomic handles.
chris: tests: add a small harness that spawns a streaming request, kills the process with SIGTERM, and verifies exporter received all spans. Put this in the infra test matrix for CI.
maya: ops + infra-bot: can we get an alert rule for exporter error rate > 0.5% and trace drop warnings?
infra-bot: noted — creating alert rule `otel.exporter.errors` and `otel.traces.dropped_rate` with 1h burn. will link PR. :robot_face:
nana: one more UX note for Console: show a per-route sampling rate and last flush latency metric so customers can see if their traces may be incomplete. small widget in the route dashboard.
devon: and docs: add a short cookbook per language detailing graceful shutdown, recommended batch defaults, required attributes, and sampling semantics.
maya: OK action items — chris to draft SDK wrapper API + batch defaults, devon to sketch language helper idioms (py/go/rust), nana to finalize attribute contract and retention policy, infra-bot to add CI harness and alerts. I'll collate and share a short RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
